svg.title: Proposed folder structure of Tell and Wire
svg.desc: The main architecture drawing with one folder per box; folders and files a cleanup would move are marked in orange.
svg.text: Proposed folder structure: each box one folder, what would move shown in orange
Same bands as the main drawing. A box with an orange frame is a folder that does not exist yet; "was ..." says where a file is now. Nothing here is done: it is the proposal.

One name, one folder per workspace
editor: graph/editor, gui/editor, backend/editor, frontend/editor. notebook: the same four, with the two extra frontend folders (gui-notebook,
graph-notebook) folded into frontend/notebook/page and /cells. authoring: graph/, gui/, backend/ authoring.
A folder is named for what is in it
backend/editor/runtime holds settings: settings/. backend/authoring holds product switching: switch/. backend/editor/graph writes with a model:
writing/. No file stands beside a folder of its own name (gui/windows.ts and gui/windows/).
Flat folders get roles, one-file folders go
host/ (12 files) into http/, session/, routes/; runtime/ (12 files) into round/, core/, services/; graph/ (12) gets run/; editor app/ (20) gets bars/
and dialogs/. deployment/gui/ (1 file) joins the session.
frontend/editor/graph: the ✨ logic is split between node/ and writing/, and views/ is the node view's: both folded. Two fields/ folders become one.
document/elements is the builders' registry: elements/. The MCP server for assistants is neither mcp/ nor ai/mcp.ts: assistant/ and ai/tools.ts.
Kinds keep one face per layer
A kind of node or block has a face in definition, authoring, runner/view and builder. That is by design (a package carries only what it runs); it stays,
and the drawing shows it as <kind>/ patterns.
Editor and notebook: what is shared
Only the model and the plumbing: graph, wiring, flow, schedule, triggers, the session, the folder, settings, ask, write, check. None needs a product
Not shared at all: the pages
The notebook imports nothing of the UI kit: its own elements, styles and look. inline.tsx and figures.ts exist twice on purpose. Keep it so.
One place that grew for both
serve.ts takes a product (a page, routes, confinement) under the name "editor", and the notebook uses it. Rename the option to product; no new code.
Watch: split when a switch appears
gui/windows/* serves the notebook and the delivered page of windows; host/browse.ts the editor and delivered tools; session.ts keeps draft or run. If
one of them needs "if notebook", give each its own file.
